messages.content: What is the freezing point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure, provided in kilopascals (kPa) or atmospheres (atm). Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The chemical name of the substance for which to calculate the boiling point, such as 'water' or 'ethanol'.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point, expressed in the unit specified by the 'unit' parameter. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the pressure value. Accepts either 'kPa' or 'atm'.

message.content:
I’m not able to compute the exact freezing point directly—there isn’t a built‑in function for that—but I can give you a good estimate based on the water phase diagram.

At 10 kPa (about 0.099 atm) the temperature where ice melts into liquid water is very close to the standard freezing point of 0 °C. In fact, the melting line rises only slightly as pressure drops from 1 atm toward the triple point (≈0.006 atm). At 10 kPa the melting point is essentially unchanged within experimental uncertainty, so you can safely assume it’s ≈ 0 °C (to within a few hundredths of a degree).

If you need a more precise value—for example, if you’re doing high‑precision cryogenic work—you’d consult detailed tables or software that interpolates the water phase diagram.
